findings.claim: The memory reservation for sessions that are admitted but not yet running (pending, M4) is computed in gatherFacts, but no test exercises it.
findings.evidence: Mutation A5 (line 486 changed to `void 0;`): admit.test.mjs gives 28 pass, 0 fail. T7 tests only decide() with a literal pending value. No check or start test has an admitted row together with a working process list and a --free-mb at which pending would change the answer.
findings.fix: Add a check-mode test: one row at active/admitted (no process, no transcript) and a candidate at active/stopped, with reserve 1024, peak 1200 and --free-mb 2300. Expect exit 6, reason memory {pending:1}. Without the admitted row, expect admitted.

findings.claim: Gate A as read from files (gateAFacts) is never exercised. Only decide() is tested, with a literal gateA object.
findings.evidence: Mutation A7 (line 357: without F5, a committed card covers only when its status is witnessed) leaves all 30 admit tests green.
findings.fix: Add a check --task test on a review row: a frozen protocol with ids [a,b], a committed card of the field covering a, and a pack with not_covered b. Expect admitted. Remove the pack entry and expect gate-a-uncovered [b]. With f5_given true and the card still pending, expect gate-a-uncovered [a,b].

findings.claim: No test covers the ce check at the start of each tick of the default-mode watcher. Without it, a quiet watcher of an old ce keeps looping, keeps holding watcher.lock and keeps rewriting watcher.json. The successor's watcher then exits 75 every time and its endturn reports watcher-missing.
findings.evidence: Mutation W3 (line 315 changed to `void 0;`): watch.test.mjs gives 61 pass, 0 fail. T15 uses --once, where runWatcher's own checkCe at line 699 fires before evaluate runs.
findings.fix: Add a test: run `watch.mjs --interval-ms 50 --no-intake` as the test's own child, raise coord.json to ce 2 after the first tick, and expect exit 64 within a bounded wait, with watcher.lock released and no watcher.json write after the raise.

findings.claim: After an owner resume, the watcher appends a new halt line at the next tick for as long as the two fails stay inside W_cc_ticks, so the resume cannot take effect for up to 30 ticks. Also, the W_cc window measured against ticks_total is untested: without it, two old fails halt the run forever.
findings.evidence: Line 489 appends a halt whenever `!runFlags.halted`, and lib.runFlags (lib.mjs 3356-3357) clears halted only through an owner resume line. Mutation W8 (line 474: `tick - f.tick < wcc` replaced by `true`) passes all three T10 tests.
findings.fix: Skip the halt append when the last owner resume is newer than the last halt that names the same fails, or when the cluster's newest fail tick is not newer than the fails recorded in the last halt line. Add tests: fails at ticks 10 and 15 with ticks_total 100 give no 26; a resume after a halt gives no second halt line.

findings.claim: stop request confirms the stop at once, with no process list and no waiting, whenever the target attempt has no bound session and no folder transcript. This frees the slot of a session the coordinator has already started but whose transcript is not visible yet. That is the typical case of parking the newest session for memory, a cut or a drop of an admitted row. R9 requires 2Δ without growth and R10 counts every live child, so this breaks both.
findings.evidence: Lines 283-309: when `att.session ?? pre.tt.folderSessions[0]` is null, the code sets stop to confirmed and step to stopped and runs dispose(), without calling proc.list(). slotCount then skips the attempt.
findings.fix: Confirm at once only when the target attempt was never admitted (no manifest). Otherwise move to stop-requested with session null and let verify sample the folder's transcripts and processes over stop_verify_deltas ticks. At minimum, refuse the immediate confirm when attemptProcesses(list,{folder}) matches or when the process list fails.

findings.claim: Intake steps run under spawnSync with no timeout. One step that never exits (for example snap.mjs --new hanging on the network) blocks the detached intake forever. The watcher sees the intake pid alive and never spawns another one, and nothing reports it.
findings.evidence: Line 817 calls spawnSync without a timeout, and step i (lines 560-570) checks only proc.alive of the intake pid.
findings.fix: Pass a timeout from a new threshold to spawnSync (it ends only its own child). Treat a timeout as exit 70: write one not-run incident {script, exit:70, timeout:true} and continue with the next step.

findings.claim: No test exercises the epoch comparison in the READY re-check (R7/M6). The test meant for it uses a READY with epoch 0, which the ready schema already rejects (minimum 1).
findings.evidence: Mutation R2 (removes `|| v.epoch !== epoch` at line 196): all 12 T5/T5b tests still pass.
findings.fix: In T5, use a schema-valid READY of another epoch ({kind:'ready', task, epoch:2} in wt/<task>-e1/staging) and expect the stall fence to apply (exit 0, epoch 2).

findings.claim: The quiescence re-check that raise makes under the lock (no row reached admitted, started or bound since the pre-check) is untested. Removing it leaves every handover test green.
findings.evidence: Mutation H4 (line 322 changed to `void 0;`): handover.test.mjs gives 18 pass, 0 fail. T5 and T7 are caught by the slotCount pre-check, so they never reach the re-check.
findings.fix: Add a seam (an exported doRaise with a beforeLock hook) so a test can move a row to admitted between the pre-check and the lock. Expect exit 6 not-quiescent, coord unchanged, one incident line.

findings.claim: No test covers the part of endturn's watcher check that requires watcher.lock to hold the pid and start time recorded in watcher.json. The impact is low.
findings.evidence: Mutation ST6 (removes the wlock conditions at line 645): T10, T11 and M1 all pass.
findings.fix: Add an endturn test: watcher.json of this ce names a live sleeper while watcher.lock is absent or names another pid. Expect exit 1 watcher-missing.

verdict: All 262 tests of the unit pass: 245 pass, 17 skipped, and every skip is an app-only test. I ran 40 mutations, at least two per script, and the tests caught 31. Of the 9 they missed, 2 are covered by an equivalent check that the tests do reach: R4 by getObject's re-hash and S4 by the compare-and-set in updateRow. The other 7 are findings: R2, A5, A7, W3 and W8, plus H4 and ST6, which matter less. Three findings are about behaviour, not test gaps. First, the watcher appends a new halt line at every tick after an owner resume while the fails stay inside W_cc (F4). Second, stop request confirms the stop of an admitted session that has no visible transcript yet, without observing anything (F5). Third, one intake step that never exits silently blocks every later intake (F6). I found no kill, no write outside the run root, no network call, no command built from untrusted text, and no wall-clock read where the design counts; the M5 pause discount is the one permitted, one-sided use. I checked the memory, reservation, slot, soft/hard, zombie and W_cc formulas by hand and they are correct. Two smaller deviations are in notes_not_findings: on first sight of a task, the watcher counts that tick toward hang (at most one tick early), and the arithmetic in spec admit T8 is wrong (the code and the test follow the rule).
